bole.text: Trunk straight and cylindrical; milky latex flows slowly from any broken part.

crown.text: Forest treelet; terminal twigs cylindrical to slightly angled, arching at the tips; branches droop less than in H. concinna.

phenology.fruit: drupe 1-1.5 cm, green turning white, its base set in the spreading red lobes of the enlarged calyx

habitat.range: Costa Rica: Puntarenas (incl. Osa Peninsula), San José, Guanacaste, Limón. Overall southern Mexico, and Costa Rica to Brazil and Bolivia (Osa Arboretum)

notes: Marginal subcanopy species. The only figure of 12 m or more is the Osa Arboretum's 'up to 15 m'. The Tree Atlas of Panama calls it a forest treelet of 5-10 m, and Manual de Plantas de Costa Rica specimens are mostly shrubs of 1-2.5 m, with two trees of 7 and 8 m. Typical height [5,10] is from the Panama atlas (src 1). Phenology is for Panama (Tree Atlas English): flowers Apr-Jul, fruit Jul-Sep; the Spanish text says Apr-Sep for both. Osa Arboretum (Costa Rica) lists flowering in Jan-Jun, Aug, Oct and Nov, with no fruiting months; Costa Rican specimens carry fruit in Jan, Mar, May, Aug, Oct and Dec. Colours disagree: the Panama atlas gives white flowers and drupes turning white; Osa gives small yellow flowers and ripe fruit dark purple on a round red calyx; Costa Rican specimens give green fruit turning purple or black, a red calyx, and flowers red, pinkish or white. A purple-black drupe on a red calyx fits the Costa Rican sources best. Family: the sources say Olacaceae; recent treatments place Heisteria in Erythropalaceae (seen only in a search result, not verified). Leaf habit is not stated. The aliases are USDA-listed synonyms seen in a search result.
